back: To go somewhere very quickly on foot or by transport.
To go quickly for a short distance (e.g., 'pop into the post office').
Fast movement, often suggesting running away from something.
To move rapidly and out of control (e.g., 'the car careered down a bank').
Other verbs suggesting very fast movement over short distances.
To move with small, rapid steps (often of animals like mice or cockroaches).
To move or fall downwards very fast.
To move upwards very fast (often used for prices or hopes).
A rapid downward movement (often in financial contexts).
To move extremely slowly (e.g., 'traffic was crawling').
To move in an unsteady or shaky way.
To walk anxiously and nervously (e.g., 'sidled up to the desk').
To move more slowly than is necessary; to waste time.
A metaphorical expression for making a major development.
